body: [A3] One-time rebuildable pipeline: Nuitka (Python) + go build (Go) -> signed package + SBOM/LBOM; release gate = no readable source. Includes build-time plug/unplug.
_note: Plane A deliver: final report persisted and status completed

brief.why: IP protection (no readable source) + supply-chain integrity (signing, SBOM/LBOM) + one source -> many editions.
brief.problem: PF must be packaged as a compiled, signed artifact with no readable source, from a one-time rebuildable pipeline.
brief.what_adds: A3 — build->package->deploy pipeline: compiled packaging (Nuitka for Python + go build for Go) + signing + SBOM/LBOM + a no-raw-.py release gate. Absorbs BI-PF-0383 (build-time plug/unplug of the worker subsystem per edition).
brief.who_feels: PF platform maintainers, workers, and customers.

label: PF Backlog 429
risks: Native C-compiler or Go toolchain absent during test runs - mitigated by verified dry-run compilation mode.
Accidental inclusion of readable Python source in customer edition packages - mitigated by fail-closed NO-RAW-.py release gate.
Subsystem exclusion prunes essential dependencies - mitigated by EAP schema dependency validation.
title: A3: PF platform build->package->deploy + compiled packaging + signing + SBOM/LBOM + NO-RAW-.py gate (absorbs BI-PF-0383)

impact_review.claim: A3 packaging pipeline consumes canonical owners without duplicate engines
NO-RAW-.py release gate enforces zero readable python source in customer editions
Build-time subsystem plug/unplug prunes modules per edition profile
API CHECK: packaging CLI and release gate invocations; no public HTTP API surface exposed directly
impact_review.recommendation: Preserve existing module API surface and CLI entry points

impact_review.claim: LANGUAGE CHECK: Python edits to core/packaging.py and core/release.py; Go compiler invocation for compiled binaries
impact_review.recommendation: Adheres to language rule for shipped modules

assumptions: Packaging execution provides dry-run/mock compilation support for test suites when native compilers are absent.
NO-RAW-.py release gate applies strictly to customer editions (enterprise, on-prem, saas, oem).
divergences: No architectural divergences; extends canonical core/packaging.py and core/release.py within existing interfaces.
prior_decisions: ADR-0001: Shipped customer editions use compiled artifacts (Go core + Nuitka compiled Python); one source, many editions; no raw .py shipped.
BI-PF-0387: Delivery baseline policy accepted; single source of truth for all editions.
BI-PF-0386: Module IP assessment 4-tier classification; 28 sensitive roots.
REL-0: Separation of distinctions (source, build, artifact, package, license, entitlement, configuration, deployment_target, runtime_policy).

context_review.reason: Existing packaging.py, signing.py, and gate modules provide clear extension points. The missing items are operational and policy decisions, not architectural blockers.
missing: Go core source status (committed or to be built)

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing components/APIs: core/code_quality_gate.py, core/deploy_providers.py, core/merge_gate.py, core/model_gate.py

approach: Wire a rebuildable pipeline that compiles Python (Nuitka) and Go (go build), signs, emits SBOM/LBOM, and fails the release gate if any raw .py is present; exclude the worker subsystem per edition at build time.

controls.control: compiled packaging pipeline builds native binary artifacts using Nuitka for Python and go build for Go
fail-closed release gate inspects packaged edition distributions and blocks raw .py files
package builder produces CycloneDX SBOM, License BOM, and cryptographic digital signatures
build-time subsystem plug/unplug mechanism prunes worker modules from customer edition packages
EAP manifest catalogs non-code asset bundles including prompt packs and UI/UX tokens

evidence:
Gate 1.5 architect review - model=gemini-2.5-flash sha=9152fbca750c
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - none
MINOR:
  - The design does not explicitly state the version pinning strategy for Nuitka and its associated C-compiler toolchain, which can lead to non-deterministic builds or compatibility issues over time.
  - While SBOM/LBOM generation is mandated, the design does not explicitly mention validation of the generated SBOM/LBOM against their respective CycloneDX/SPDX schemas, which would enhance robustness.
  - The design mentions cryptographic digital signatures but lacks details on the key management lifecycle (e.g., rotation, revocation, secure storage) for the signing keys, which is critical for long-term security.
NIT:
  - The `config/eap-registry.json` is a critical configuration artifact; consider adding a specific versioning strategy for its schema changes beyond just "fully backward-compatible" to manage evolution more formally.
SUMMARY:
  - none
RECOMMENDATION: no hard blocker (MAJOR/MINOR/NIT advisory; HIL decides)

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=gemini-2.5-flash sha=d30dbae049c1
BLOCKER:
  - AC-1 Not Met: The `build_compiled_package` function only creates mock binaries, directly violating the acceptance criterion for building native binary artifacts using Nuitka and Go.
  - Security: Shipping mock binaries instead of genuinely compiled code undermines the security and IP protection goals of compiled packaging, creating a false sense of security.
MAJOR:
  - AC-3 Not Fully Compliant: The SBOM schema `CycloneDX/SPDX-productforge@1` is a custom schema, not a standard CycloneDX or SPDX compliant one as required by the acceptance criteria.
  - Language Rule Violation: New core orchestration logic for packaging, SBOM/LBOM, and subsystem exclusion is implemented in Python (`core/packaging.py`), which contradicts the "new shipped logic -> Go" standard.
MINOR:
  - Hardcoded Customer Editions: The `customer_editions` list is duplicated in `packaging.py` and `release.py`, which should be consolidated into a shared constant for maintainability.
  - Missing `dry_run` usage: The `dry_run` parameter in `build_compiled_package` is passed but not utilized to control the mock binary creation, reducing its intended utility.
  - Broad Exception Handling: `attach_sbom_and_signatures` uses a broad `except Exception as e`, which can mask specific issues and hinder debugging.
NIT:
  - Magic String for Mock Binary: The mock binary content `b"\x7fELF\x02\x01\x01_COMPILED_PF_BINARY_A3"` is a magic string; defining it as a constant would improve readability.
  - Redundant `list()` calls: In `eap_build`, `list(exclude_subsystems or [])` and `list(asset_bundles or [])` are redundant if the input types are already lists or None.
SUMMARY:
  - none
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=gemini-2.5-flash sha=61ae5027bdeb
BLOCKER:
  - AC-1 Not Fully Met: The Nuitka compilation step targets only `core/release.py`, which does not fulfill the requirement to compile "Python modules" (plural) or "All shipped Python modules" as stated in the design. This will lead to AC-2's `no_raw_py_gate` failing the build for other uncompiled Python source files.
MAJOR:
  - none
MINOR:
  - `test_subsystem_plug_unplug_workers` removes `as tmpdir` from `TemporaryDirectory` context manager, but the variable was not used, making it a minor cleanup.
NIT:
  - none
SUMMARY:
  - none
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=gemini-2.5-flash sha=7ee2746cdc0b
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - AC-1 / FR-1: Compilation failure for individual Python modules does not abort the package build, violating the design contract.
  - AC-1 / FR-1: If a module fails to compile, it is simply omitted from artifacts without an explicit error or build failure.
MINOR:
  - The `os.listdir` approach with `not f.startswith("__")` for `core` modules is a heuristic that might be brittle if `core` contains non-shippable Python files in the future.
NIT:
  - Removal of `signing` and `bom` imports from `test_a3_packaging.py` is a cleanup, assuming `packaging` orchestrates these and the test does not directly assert on them.
SUMMARY:
  - none
RECOMMENDATION: no hard blocker (MAJOR/MINOR/NIT advisory; HIL decides)

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=gemini-2.5-flash sha=447230c75df0
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - none
MINOR:
  - none
NIT:
  - none
SUMMARY:
  - The change directly resolves prior MAJOR findings regarding compilation failure handling, significantly improving build pipeline integrity.
  - Explicit error reporting on Nuitka compilation failure enhances observability and maintainability.
  - This modification aligns well with robust enterprise packaging standards and the design contract.
RECOMMENDATION: no hard blocker (MAJOR/MINOR/NIT advisory; HIL decides)

requirements.title: Concrete A3 Compiled Packaging Orchestration
requirements.errors: Compilation failure or missing required artifacts aborts package build with explicit error.
requirements.outputs: compiled package distribution structure and updated packaging manifest
requirements.trigger: Packaging build execution via API or CLI.
requirements.acceptance: Given a build request for an edition, when running A3 packaging, then native binary artifacts are produced with zero readable Python source files.
requirements.data_rules: All shipped Python modules compiled to C-extensions (.pyd/.so); Go modules compiled to native binaries.
requirements.edge_cases: Handling platforms where native C-compiler is absent in CI dry-run environments.
requirements.idempotency: Repeated build runs overwrite previous build outputs deterministically.
requirements.preconditions: Delivery baseline BI-PF-0387 and module IP inventory BI-PF-0386 are active.

requirements.title: Fail-Closed NO-RAW-.py Release Gate
requirements.errors: Any uncompiled .py file in a customer edition immediately fails closed with UNMET: RAW_PY_IN_SHIPPED_PACKAGE.
requirements.inputs: packaged artifact directory or file manifest
requirements.outputs: pass/fail gate verdict with violating file paths if any
requirements.trigger: Release gate evaluation or precheck execution.
requirements.acceptance: Given a packaged customer edition, when inspected by the NO-RAW-.py gate, then the release is approved only if no raw .py files exist in the distribution.
requirements.data_rules: Shipped customer editions (enterprise, on-prem, saas, oem) must contain exactly 0 raw .py files.
requirements.edge_cases: Distinguishing between customer editions and community/dev edition.
requirements.preconditions: Packaging output directory or archive is generated.

requirements.title: Automated SBOM, LBOM, and Digital Signing Emission
requirements.errors: Missing SBOM or invalid signature material blocks package completion.
requirements.inputs: package footprint, dependencies, and signing credentials
requirements.outputs: sbom.json, lbom.json, checksums.txt, and detached digital signature
requirements.acceptance: Given compiled package artifacts, when final packaging runs, then compliant SBOM, LBOM, and checksum manifests are attached.
requirements.data_rules: SHA-256 checksums generated for all package files; licenses mapped to SPDX standards.
requirements.edge_cases: Graceful handling when GPG key is absent in test environments by recording unsigned status.
requirements.idempotency: Deterministic SBOM and checksum generation matching artifact bytes.

requirements.title: Build-Time Subsystem Plug/Unplug (Absorbing BI-PF-0383)
requirements.errors: Attempting to exclude mandatory core subsystems (e.g. licensing or auth) is rejected.
requirements.inputs: edition profile and subsystem exclusion flags (e.g. exclude_workers)
requirements.outputs: pruned package manifest and distribution archive excluding designated subsystem
requirements.acceptance: Given an edition configured with exclude_workers=True, when packaging completes, then all worker fleet modules are excluded from the distribution package.
requirements.data_rules: Excluded modules and their dependencies are completely pruned from the compiled archive.
requirements.edge_cases: Ensuring orchestrator remains functional when workers are unplugged.
requirements.idempotency: Predictable module exclusion based on declarative edition profile.
requirements.preconditions: Edition profile specifies subsystem inclusion/exclusion list.

requirements.title: Future-Proof Asset Bundle Cataloging
requirements.errors: Tampered or unmanifested asset bundles fail EAP validation.
requirements.inputs: asset bundles (prompt packs, UI/UX tokens, web console)
requirements.outputs: EAP manifest containing verified asset bundle records
requirements.acceptance: Given prompt and UI/UX asset bundles, when EAP builds, then all asset bundles are registered and validated alongside code artifacts.
requirements.data_rules: Assets carry checksum, format, and destination metadata.
requirements.edge_cases: Handling editions that omit optional asset bundles.
requirements.idempotency: Deterministic cataloging of non-code asset bundles.
